Can footage narrow down which recipe filled each vial?

2. Liquid level

We compare 34 unlabeled vials from Videos 1–4 with 10 labeled recipe references from Video 5.

3separate methods, then an evidence review
Say: We will show what each of the three methods can tell us, where it fails, and then the candidate recipe for every one of the 34 unlabeled vials.
VIDEO 5 • ONE CLEAN VIAL IMAGE PER RECIPE

Our reference: 10 labeled recipes

Each photo is paired with the labeled tank volumes. Open the full-size image to inspect all ten recipes.
Say: These ten labeled Video 5 recipes are the reference library. Videos 1–4 have no authoritative recipe labels, so every ID we assign to them remains a candidate.
COLOR FINGERPRINT • NEAREST LAB-SPACE RECIPE REFERENCES

Method 1 | Match the finished-liquid color

Video 5 holdout: color top-1 16/20, top-2 18/20Within this one recording; not cross-run accuracy.
Each vial photo shows its closest and next-closest color reference. Lower Lab distance means closer; it is not a probability. Examples of close alternatives: R14 can rank R7 second; an R12 test vial ranked R13 second.
Say: Color is the most useful single cue so far: it ranked 16 of 20 clean Video 5 repeats first and 18 in the top two. But look at the runner-up too: similar colors and lighting make a single exact ID risky.
HEIGHT CUE • RECIPE VOLUME GRAPH AND VIAL EVIDENCE

Method 2 | Use liquid level as a volume clue

What the level images show

Recipe 5 · 30 mL

T100: 10 mL + T200: 10 mL + T400: 10 mL

Visible meniscus; estimated image height 71–96 px.

Recipe 8 · 60 mL

T100: 20 mL + T200: 20 mL + T400: 20 mL

Meniscus range is behind the holder; not directly visible.

Recipe 9 · 80 mL

T100: 10 mL + T200: 35 mL + T400: 35 mL

Meniscus range is behind the holder; not directly visible.

Across the 34 unlabeled vials: 3 appear low; 31 have hidden/uncertain menisci. Separate Video 5 holdout: level top-1 2/4, top-2 4/4 when visible (4/20 clean vials).
This flags a possible low-fill conflict for Video 3 vials 4–6, but does not produce recipe IDs. Holder obstruction and no pixel-to-mL calibration are the main limits.
Say: Level only helped on a handful of visible examples. In the 34-vial set, just three are flagged as possibly low and the other 31 cannot be measured confidently; in the separate labeled holdout only four of twenty levels were visible.
NOZZLE APPEARANCE • AUTOMATIC PHASES ARE HEURISTIC

Method 3 | Follow orange/blue stream sequences

50heuristic phase detections across 34 vials
5/34with no orange/blue phase detected

Separate Video 5 holdout: stream top-1 4/20, top-2 10/20.

Sequences can reveal a repeated visual pattern, but a detected hue is not proof of which tank flowed.

Short phases, reflections, mixed hues, clear flow, and missed intervals all affect the result. Video 5 exact expected colored order was observed in only 8 of 30 labeled windows.

Open/download the annotated clip
Say: The stream view adds process context, but it is the noisiest cue: the automatic labels are only appearance candidates. The held-out score and incomplete sequences show why we should not let it override the vial color by itself.

Videos 1–4 have no labels, so their accuracy cannot be measured. “Combined reading” keeps the color top match as a candidate, flags level conflicts, and reports stream evidence without forcing an unvalidated fusion score.
Say: Here is the per-vial answer: color supplies a ranked candidate and runner-up; stream sequence and visible level add context. Video 2 consistently points to R11, Video 4 separates a blue-looking group from a dark teal group, and Video 3's R14-like color conflicts with low-level observations on its last three vials. These are hypotheses until checked against batch records.
